# nonSymbol

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a symbol.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonSymbol() — Checks whether a value is **not** a symbol. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.4.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonSymbol<T>(value: T | symbol): value is T;
```

`nonSymbol(value)` is the same test as `!isSymbol(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Registered symbols from `Symbol.for` and the well-known symbols both pass; nothing else does.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| symbol` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a symbol; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonSymbol("id"); // => true
nonSymbol(null); // => true
nonSymbol(Symbol("id")); // => false
nonSymbol(Symbol.iterator); // => false
```
